correctness.rationale: This passes the repaired statement. The frozen proof omitted the change of model: the first tabulated line y+ez=0 is not a bitangent in the cyclic coordinates, where restriction has a simple zero at (1:0:0). In the cited Ciani coordinates the quartic is x^4+y^4+z^4+3e(x^2y^2+x^2z^2+y^2z^2), the Klein member of the pencil. Both plane quartic embeddings are canonical; their projective equivalence carries the entire incidence graph. I checked all 28 binary-quartic restrictions on the symmetric model over the quadratic field; each has even intersection multiplicities. I matched the 21 reflection-line equations to Gévay–Pokora §2.1 and independently reconstructed both incidence graphs by exact concurrent-triple determinants, recovering the intersection counts and checking the labelled bijection on both entire edge sets. The simple zero of the characteristic polynomial ensures connectedness. Two independent incidence minors have determinant 2^18 3^23 7^5 and prime-local elimination gives 36 units and twelve nonunits 2^4, 18, 54, 108, 756^5 (multiplicities). The repair corrects the frozen proof's count of eleven and notes why the mod-two quotient forces at least twelve generators. The geometry is invariant under coordinates, so the corrected proof retains the asserted cyclic-model graph rather than computing a different object.
residual_risks: The finite computation uses characteristic-zero geometry; it does not establish reduction behavior or a statement about the algebraic Jacobian of the Klein quartic.

value.rationale: This is the complete flag graph of the classical bitangent/fourfold-crossing configuration and hence a natural named geometric incidence object. The integral chip-firing group, its exponent and its generation rank make precise the divisor-class obstructions on that graph, independently of which known geometric model is used. Those obstructions would not be provided by the incidence or tree count alone or by the closely related quadruple-only group.
residual_risks: The result concerns the one named graph, not an algebraic Jacobian or a family-wide critical-group classification.
